one_month_reasoning: Cause of today's drop, verified: not company-specific. Vistra filed no 8-K on Oct 13-14 (EDGAR feed; last 8-K Oct 5, a credit-facility amendment). BLS September CPI (released Oct 14): +0.6% m/m, +3.7% y/y, core +0.3% m/m and +2.6% y/y, energy +5.2% m/m; the supervisor confirmed these actuals at BLS. Debt-heavy AI infrastructure sold off (CoreWeave -16%, Oracle -9%; S&P 500 -1.3%, Nasdaq -1.9%) and the AI-power IPPs fell together (VST -6.7%, TLN -6.2%, NRG -5.9%, CEG -5.6%) while the utilities index fell ~0.5%: a sector move set off by a market-wide macro print, after a ~20% run in early October. Fair value is unchanged by it. Window events to Nov 13: PJM Members Committee Oct 22 and RBP refiling Oct 29 (new-build procurement and cost allocation; no cap on existing plants in play); FOMC Oct 27-28 (a hike would extend the rate-led derating); hyperscaler Q3 results and 2027 capex guides late October; Vistra Q3 on Nov 6 with the 2026/2027 guidance update - the CFO already said 2027 is trending to the low end of $7.4-7.8B before ~$0.7B from Cogentrix/Meta, so an ~$8.1B frame is largely expected, and a print below it is the main downside in the window. I drop the round-1 upward tilt from VST's own post -6% day history (a 2023-25 bull-run sample; context only per the supervisor) and keep only a ~1% drift (equity premium plus mild short-term reversal). Distribution: lognormal, median $153.5, sigma 15.5% (50% annual vol / 3.5 = 14.3%, widened for the Nov 6 earnings event and the FOMC).

thesis_break_reason: At $112 pro forma equity (112 x ~340.6M shares incl. the 5.0M Cogentrix shares = $38.1B) plus pro forma net claims (~$25.4B = $21.6B incl. preferred + $2.3B Cogentrix cash + $1.5B assumed debt) is ~$63.5B, ~7.8x the $8.1B 2027 base: ~1.1x below NRG (8.9x), the cheapest IPP, ~2x below VST's own ~9.8x today, and ~16% under the 52-week low ($132.66). That only makes sense if a fundamental leg breaks: (a) the flagged trigger, a PJM move to cap or administratively set capacity prices for 2030/31+ - status 2026-10-14: NOT tripped; the ~$325/~$175 collar covers RPM auctions only through 2029/2030 (PJM answer ER26-1556, source 31; FERC accepted 2026-04-28, source 16), PJM evaluates incentives with stakeholders by end-2026 and then sets the 2030/31+ path, and the Reliability Backstop Procurement was accepted and suspended to 2027-02-28 with a new FERC section 206 proceeding (source 18) - it procures new build rather than capping existing plants, and no filing to extend the cap was found; (b) the Nov 6 guidance update putting 2027 well below $8.1B including deals; or (c) a hyperscaler contract failing. I keep $112 rather than the supervisor's $115: at 50% realized vol, $115-130 is reachable on rates/AI-factor moves alone (the stock fell 6.5% today on CPI with no company news).

reverse_dcf_check: Engine: the 9.25x NTM adjusted EV/EBITDA leg ($168.3) implies a WACC of ~8.6% against my 9.37%, with 2.5% perpetual growth after FY2030, ~37.7% adjusted EBITDA margins (EBIT ~27.2%) and capex at 11% of revenue vs D&A 10.5%. So a horizon buyer at 9.25x accepts ~0.75pt less return than my DCF requires, or equivalently prices ~3% long-run growth at my WACC. That is plausible only if PJM keeps market-based capacity pricing after 2029/30 and ERCOT load arrives; with a 0.4 probability of a 2030/31+ cap (~-$1.8/share) and 0.35 of prolonged ERCOT softness (~-$2.3/share), I keep the multiple 1.35x under the peer median and the DCF at 30% weight as the check on it.
